Timeheld Beta Privacy Policy

Version
1.4
Effective date
October 30, 2026
Covers
The Timeheld private beta distributed through Apple TestFlight only

1. Who we are

Timeheld is operated by Jan Kazimierczak ("Timeheld", "we", "us"). We are responsible for (the "controller" of) the personal information described here. Contact: support@timeheld.app.

2. What this policy covers

This policy covers only the private beta of Timeheld that we invite you to test through Apple TestFlight, on Mac, iPhone and iPad. It does not cover visits to the timeheld.app website, and the public version of Timeheld will have its own privacy policy. This policy works together with the Timeheld Private Beta Tester Agreement you sign. The beta is only for invited testers aged 18 or over living in Canada (outside Quebec) or the EU, and we do not knowingly collect information from anyone younger.

3. What Apple collects through TestFlight

Apple's privacy policy and TestFlight & Privacy notice (apple.com/legal/privacy/data/en/test-flight) cover what Apple collects. Apple automatically collects crash logs and usage information while you test (you cannot turn this off) and shares with us: your name and invitation email and invitation status; your device model and a device identifier, OS version, language and installed beta version; the number of sessions, installs and crashes and crash logs; and any feedback you choose to send (screenshots and comments) with technical details such as time zone, connection type, battery level and free disk space. Apple does not give us your device names. Apple says it keeps feedback for one year and may keep crash and usage data until bugs are resolved. Manage your data held by Apple at privacy.apple.com.

4. What the beta app uses, and where it goes

  • On your device and in your own private iCloud: your study sessions and hours, courses, timer plans and blocked website domains are stored on your device. They can sync, with your session status and device registrations, through your own private iCloud (Apple CloudKit). Sync is on by default on Mac and off by default on iPhone and iPad (Sync across devices in Settings), and stays off if you switched it off; an active restriction you set may delay turning it off, and data already uploaded stays in iCloud. Separately from Sign in with Apple, the app must link your device's iCloud account to Timeheld before it syncs any study data: you confirm this on the sign-in screen ("Sign in and confirm iCloud sync in one step"), with Confirm iCloud sync in Settings if the link is missing or your iCloud account changed, and, after an account deletion, before a device that was never linked syncs again. We have no access to this data through iCloud or our account service; we see it only if you share it, for example in screenshots, exports or emails.
  • Screen Time selections stay on your device. The apps you choose to block are stored as coded tokens from Apple and are not synced or sent to us.
  • Safari extension (the only browser extension in this beta): it checks web addresses against your block list on your device and does not send your browsing history, page titles or page content to us.
  • Our account service (Supabase): you sign in with Sign in with Apple. The app does not ask Apple for your name or email, but if an email was shared with Timeheld through an earlier sign-in, the account service may still hold it. The service processes the sign-in token from Apple and stores: an account ID linked to your Apple sign-in, a support ID, a random installation ID, platform, a generic device label (such as "My iPhone"), app version, your access plan (Test Free or Test Premium, which you switch in Settings; there is no code entry), a log of account events, and dates such as when your account or devices were created, last seen or retired, or your access changed. For deletion, it receives a one-time code from Apple and keeps an encrypted Apple token until the deletion is finished or we remove it; meanwhile your account is paused. Our hosting provider also keeps sign-in security logs (which can include your account ID, IP address and device or browser information) only as long as needed to protect accounts and investigate misuse.
  • No additional advertising, tracking, analytics or crash-reporting tools beyond Apple's TestFlight services. We do not sell your information or use it for advertising.
  • Other records: your signed Tester Agreement (name, Apple Account email, country, age confirmation, signature, date), emails you send to support@timeheld.app, and any study content or personal information you include in feedback, screenshots or support messages.

5. Why we use it and our legal basis

We use your information to run your account, give you access to the beta and manage the Tester Agreement (EU legal basis: contract, GDPR Art. 6(1)(b)); to fix and improve Timeheld using TestFlight crash reports, diagnostics and your feedback; and to keep Timeheld secure and keep proof of the Tester Agreement in case of a legal claim (EU legal basis for both: legitimate interests, Art. 6(1)(f)). In Canada, we rely on your consent, which you give by joining the beta. You can withdraw it at any time (section 9), but you may then no longer be able to test the beta.

6. Who we share it with

Only our service providers: Apple (TestFlight, iCloud, Sign in with Apple and Apple Push Notification service), Supabase (hosting of our account service), Google (Gmail, which we use to receive support email and to email testers) and Namecheap (email forwarding for support@timeheld.app), plus authorities if the law requires it. Signed Tester Agreements are kept on our own computer, not with a third-party service. Apple does not allow us to share TestFlight data with third parties, and we don't.

7. International transfers

We are based in Canada. Our account service's database is set up in Supabase's Canada Central region, but our providers (Apple, Supabase, Google and Namecheap) may process some data, such as logs or support email, in other countries under their own terms and safeguards. If you live in the EU, you provide your information directly to us in Canada. The European Commission recognises Canada as providing adequate protection for personal information handled by organisations subject to Canada's federal private-sector privacy law (PIPEDA) in the course of commercial activities.

8. How long we keep it

  • Account service data: while your account exists. In the app, Delete account deletes your account and its records from the account service, asks Apple to revoke Timeheld's Sign in with Apple access and clears your Timeheld study content from your private iCloud. Deletion must wait until an active session or current sleep block ends. Settings needed for an existing 48-hour restriction commitment may remain until that commitment ends and cleanup can finish. Updated offline devices clear their associated study data after reconnecting and confirming deletion, once active protection permits cleanup. Connectivity or service errors can delay completion; interrupted deletion can be resumed from account settings. A few small records stay in your private iCloud holding only a deletion marker with a one-way hash of your account ID, so other devices don't restore old data; they are not removed automatically (you can delete Timeheld's data in Apple's iCloud settings). Each device also keeps its installation ID and an account hash, and iPhone and iPad keep a restriction-commitment file. A hashed deletion receipt, with no account ID, Apple ID or email, is used to confirm the deletion for 30 days; it may stay in our database after that until it is removed when a later deletion is processed.
  • By email: you can ask at support@timeheld.app for help with deletion. We handle these manually and can delete your account data from the account service; data on your devices and in your iCloud is cleared only through the app's deletion flow or by you. You can also stop using Sign in with Apple for Timeheld at any time in your Apple Account settings.
  • Signed Tester Agreement: until 3 years after your confidentiality obligations under section 7 of the agreement end (at the latest 2 years after your participation ends if Timeheld has not launched publicly). Then we keep only your name, the date and the version signed while we rely on the feedback licence or no-copying promise, reviewed yearly.
  • TestFlight data: Apple keeps it as described in section 3; we do not download or keep it outside App Store Connect.
  • Support emails: as long as needed to answer you, then deleted within 12 months.
  • Other copies: provider logs and backups follow the providers' own terms; exported files and copies on your devices stay until you delete them.

9. Your rights

You can ask us to access, correct or delete your information, to receive a copy in a portable format, and to withdraw your consent. If you live in the EU, you can also restrict or object to our use of it. Email support@timeheld.app. We respond without undue delay and within the legal deadline: for EU requests, generally one month (where the law allows an extension, we explain why within that month), and for Canadian requests, 30 days. We may need to keep some information, such as the signed agreement, where the law allows (section 8).

If you are not satisfied, you can complain to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada (priv.gc.ca) or, in the EU, to the data protection supervisory authority where you live.

10. Security, changes and contact

Timeheld uses Sign in with Apple and encrypted HTTPS. Each device stores its local copy of sign-in credentials in that device's Keychain. Our account service also processes authentication tokens and stores the account identifiers described in section 4; unfinished deletion may retain an encrypted Apple revocation token. Cached account and access validation can remain valid offline for up to 72 hours, subject to earlier access-grant expiry. You may need to reconnect to refresh access; existing protection commitments can continue. No system is completely secure; we will tell you and the authorities about any breach as the law requires. We will email you about important changes to this policy before they take effect. Questions: support@timeheld.app.

Changes from version 1.3: we shortened the description of how the app works with Apple services in section 4. Nothing else changed.
